_comment: Asserted byte sizes for istor.fyi's artifact. verify-budget.py fails the build when any of these moves, so a regenerated crop or re-subset font cannot quietly make the site heavier than SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §12.1 says it is. Updating a number here is meant to be a deliberate two-file commit: this file and the design plan's table. Values were measured from disk on 2026-09-19, not transcribed.

totals._note: The payload SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §12.1 prints as 452 KB / 704 KB of exhibits. The plan's table is an estimate carried from the specification; these are the measured values, and on 2026-09-19 the plan's table was re-baselined to match them — the two are one commit. phone_1x is the 1x ASSET payload (exports + ground + the three fonts) and deliberately excludes the document, which is asserted separately under `document` below.

document._note: The design plan's payload table omits the document. index.html is real weight and it arrives first, so it is asserted here rather than merely reported. Two numbers, asserted two different ways, and the difference is deliberate. index_html_bytes is a property of the DOCUMENT alone — the artifact is LF-only, so it is identical on every platform — and it is asserted exactly: an edit to the copy deck, or to the stylesheet's CODE rather than its comments, moves it and is meant to. index_html_gzip_ceiling is a property of the document AND of the zlib that compressed it, and Python does not promise byte-stable output across versions, so it is a ceiling with room in it. HISTORY. It read 18,051 B gzipped off 44,812 B raw for all of v1. On 2026-09-19 the first CI run failed a document it had not touched — the artifact was byte-identical to the reviewed one and only the compressed figure differed, 13,722 B on CI's Python 3.12.14/Linux against 13,772 B here on 3.14/Windows, off the same input. A gate that fails on the compressor rather than on the site teaches its reader to ignore it, so the exactness moved to the number that can carry it. RE-BASELINE FOR V2. Both numbers moved: 62,543 B raw, 18,046 B gzipped. The document grew by 17,657 B because the page did — v1 was a static essay with three bitmaps and v2 is twelve acts. The growth is itemised, and none of it is accidental: the inline stylesheet went 15,054 B of code to 19,890 B (five compositions instead of one, a replica window, an accordion, a ring plate, and the motion block), and the markup went roughly 28 KB to 39 KB (the hero's live DOM replica, which is what lets the page perform the product rather than show a picture of it, plus a second smaller replica in the close, which is what Thoria chose over a bitmap there, plus seven FAQ items). The 4,866 B poster replica is the largest single addition and it is a decision, not drift. The compression ratio did NOT get worse — 30.7% under v1, 28.9% now — so this is a longer document, not a harder one, which is what the ceiling is here to distinguish. The ceiling sits 373 B over the highest figure seen, 2.1%, about five times the 50 B spread measured between the two toolchains: room for a zlib to differ, not for the document to change. It is the compression this check fixes, not the compression a visitor receives — GitHub Pages sets that — so this is a floor on the document's weight and a tripwire on it changing. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the Act 8 clearance). 67,326 B to 67,340 B raw; the ceiling holds, at 19,150 B measured against 19,350 B. The 14 B is one declaration: `.plate-inner`'s `padding-block-start` moved from a fixed `150px` to `calc(13.5% + 56px)`, which is 13 B of longer value and 1 B for the blank line the edit left above the rule. That the document moved by exactly that much, and by nothing else, was measured rather than assumed: this build's own `inline_css()` was run over `HEAD:Source/styles.css` and over the working copy, and the diff of the two stripped stylesheets is that one declaration. The raw figure is what moved, so the raw figure is what was re-baselined. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the ring's holes become visible). 67,340 B to 67,544 B raw (+204) and the gzip ceiling 19,350 B to 19,650 B, against 19,242 B measured. The +204 is 203 B of inlined figure and 1 B of stylesheet: `calendar-ring.svg` went 1,318 B to 1,521 B because the dashed circle's stroke changed from `var(--rule)` to `var(--ink-3)` and the two comments that explain it grew with it, and `.plate-inner`'s clearance moved `13.5%` to `24%`. The ceiling MOVED UP for the first time, and deliberately: it existed as a floor on the document's weight with room for a compressor to differ rather than for the document to change, it sat 108 B over the measured figure after this change, and 108 B is under three of the 50 B toolchain spreads it was sized to absorb. It is now 2.1% over the measurement again, the same margin it carried when it was written, so it keeps meaning what it meant. A ceiling that is silently eroded by successive re-baselines stops being a tripwire, which is why this one is recorded rather than nudged. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the reading list). 67,544 B to 71,933 B raw, and the ceiling 19,650 B to 20,480 B against 20,300 B measured. The +4,389 raw is the close's new footer: sixteen links into the carried library, four column heads, a lede, and the comment that explains the block. The ceiling moved to a ROUND number on purpose, 20 KiB, rather than to another 2.1% margin. Three re-baselines in one night is the signal: a ceiling that has to be edited on every commit that touches the document is not guarding the compressor any more, it is tracking the document, and the exact raw assertion above already does that job. At a round 20 KiB it is 180 B over this measurement and will not need touching again until something adds a tenth of a document at once, which is the class of change it exists to catch. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the markup stops shipping its comments). 71,933 B to 63,175 B raw, a **fall of 8,758 B**, and the ceiling 20,480 B to 18,432 B against 17,519 B measured. The fall is one build change: `Source/index.html` carried 21 html comments, 7,768 B, 18.3% of the document, and every visitor downloaded them. Gzipped they were 2,348 B of 12,249, or 19% of the compressed document, which is the number that says they were not trivia. The stylesheet had already solved this exact problem and said so in the header it ships, so this is that rule finally reaching the file it was never applied to. `Source/index.html` still carries all 21 comments; nothing was deleted, only unshipped. The ceiling came DOWN with the measurement rather than staying loose: 20 KiB was sized for a 71 KB document whose tenth is 2 KB gzipped, and at 17.5 KB it would have stopped being able to see that class of change. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (C1 becomes full-bleed). The raw tripwire moved 63,175 B to 65,447 B and the ceiling did NOT move: 18,085 B measured against 18,432 B, 347 B of room, 1.9%, the same margin the round 20 KiB figure was sized with. The +2,272 was measured rather than reasoned about, by rebuilding HEAD into a throwaway tree (`git archive HEAD Source Assets OldVersion`, then the build) and diffing the two artifacts: HEAD builds 64,249 B raw and 17,842 B gzipped, the working tree builds 65,447 B and 18,085 B, so this change is +1,198 raw and +243 gzipped. The other +1,074 raw was ALREADY IN HEAD AND ALREADY FAILING THIS ASSERTION. The parallax commit shipped it, and the budget was read through a pipe, so the exit code that came back belonged to grep and not to the verifier: a gate whose failure can be lost in a pipeline reports ok when it is not. This re-baseline therefore covers two commits, and the second is the one worth looking at, 1,074 B of unexamined document against 1,198 B of examined. +46 B, same night, same act: `html` gains `scrollbar-color: var(--ink-3) transparent`, because the UA's white scrollbar track was a bright stripe down the right edge of a first screen that is now deep teal. One declaration, 11 B gzipped, and the comment above it is stripped like every other stylesheet comment. RE-BASELINE AND RE-SIZE, 2026-09-19 (the rail becomes a table of contents). Raw 65,493 B to 66,726 B (+1,233) and the ceiling 18,432 B to 20,480 B, against 18,417 B measured. This is the first time the ceiling has had to MOVE UP rather than merely be re-measured, and it needs justifying, because a ceiling that is raised whenever it is reached is not a ceiling. It was 18,432 B because the document was 17,519 B when the shipped-comment change landed, and 18 KiB was the round number about a tenth above that. The document is now 18,417 B, so the same rule gives a round 20 KiB again: the ceiling returns to the value it held before the comment change, which is the honest way to read it, one ceiling re-sized twice rather than a number being chased. What forced it was not this change but this change's last byte: it left FIFTEEN bytes of room, and the measured spread between two toolchains compressing the same input is around fifty. A ceiling inside the compressor's own noise fails a document nobody touched, which is the failure this file's history already contains once. It is also worth saying what the +1,233 is: 1,187 B of inlined stylesheet code (the rail's pill, which is real shipped code) plus 46 B of document. The script that drives the rail is inside the document and is most of the rest; its reasoning is in a comment that does not ship.

library._note: The carried library (SITE_BUILD_PLAN.md §5). Pages are asserted as a count and a total, not file by file — their bytes change the moment anyone edits a summary, and 75 rows of page sizes would assert nothing worth failing over. Shared assets are exact.
